It has long been common practice in the field of electronics, when seeking to characterize an unknown circuit or device, to use a technique known as reflectometry. This technique involves sending a known signal into the circuit or device and then observing the signal that is reflected back. By analyzing the reflected signal, one can gain insights into the characteristics and behavior of the circuit or device. Reflectometry is particularly useful for analyzing the behavior of circuits and devices that operate at extremely high frequencies, such as those at millimeter wavelength frequencies. These frequencies, typically ranging from 30 GHz to 300 GHz, are of great interest for high-speed data communications, radar, and other high-speed electronic applications.
